extracted.intended_audience: managers and functional specialists in Canadian federal departments and agencies responsible for regulatory consultation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, conducting, evaluating, and documenting federal regulatory consultations in Canada, including required components of consultation plans, participant selection, tools, timelines, budgeting, evaluation, and officials' skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials conducting the consultations should be open to stakeholders’ views and opinions and should take these into account in preparing the proposed regulations. They should be impartial with respect to the views expressed and willing to allow them to influence the final version of the proposed regulations, if appropriate. If some aspects of the proposal are not subject to change, this should be clearly communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity regarding the purpose and objectives of the consultation and the proposed regulations is essential; communicate which aspects are not subject to change so participants can focus efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and balance
rubrics_metrics.description: All stakeholders, whether directly or indirectly affected, should have an opportunity to contribute their views. Significant effort should be made to identify the 'most affected stakeholders.' Officials should ensure that an appropriate balance of views is represented in the consultation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make efforts to identify and include both directly and indirectly affected parties to achieve balanced input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The relationship between the department and stakeholders should be transparent. Officials should ensure transparency of the overall regulatory consultation process, pertinent non-sensitive information, the decision-making process, and how stakeholder input will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency builds trust; document and communicate process, information made available, decision steps, and use of input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments should demonstrate accountability by documenting how the views of stakeholders were considered during the development of the regulations and informing stakeholders of how those views were used. Where stakeholder input could not be reflected in the proposed regulations, officials should be able to outline the reason(s) why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records showing how input was considered; allow reasonable time for participation; report back and explain decisions when input is not incorporated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation Plan (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear and comprehensive consultation plan that frames the boundaries of the consultation process, states objectives, issues under review, public environment analysis, key participants, timelines, mechanisms for reporting results, proposed approach, and 'rules of engagement.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite stakeholder input on the plan where appropriate; scale plan to expected impact/scope; use terms of reference for ongoing committees; for routine/low-impact proposals a detailed plan may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of purpose and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation plan should begin with a clear statement of the purpose and objectives: explain the problem the proposed regulations address; present a compelling argument for government intervention; explain why regulation is the tool of choice; be broad enough for views but precise enough to keep discussion centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items to include: explain problem; explain why regulations are being developed (economic/social/safety benefits); define what proposed regulations will do; describe how regulations will be developed (process); outline consultation scope (what can/cannot be considered); identify authority for the regulations; be written in plain, easy-to-understand language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public environment analysis — internal scan
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an internal analysis to confirm senior management and ministerial support, policy approval, and consistency with government priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items: determine senior management’s commitment; confirm ministerial support; determine appropriate policy authority; assess consistency with government priorities; research emerging legislation, policy, or litigation that could affect the consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public environment analysis — external scan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess level of public and media interest, potential stakeholder positions, possible conflicts, and communications challenges; use this to determine scope, tools, and triage of the consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items include: determine public interest; examine public perception; assess stakeholders’ perceptions; review past positions of stakeholders; determine whether issue is contentious; assess social/economic/health/environmental impacts; examine parliamentary committee and independent body reports; assess provincial/territorial/municipal views; review previous lobbying; assess trade-offs and distributional impacts; identify similar approaches by other governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing realistic timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Timelines should identify activities and milestones for all consultative aspects, be flexible for unforeseen circumstances, and allow sufficient time for stakeholders to become informed, consult, and respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve stakeholders in setting timelines where possible; ensure consultations occur early enough to allow for drafting, approvals, pre-publication, and parliamentary schedules. Checklist items: assess stakeholder knowledge; determine information needs; select appropriate time of year; assess deadlines for decision making; factor timing of other regulatory steps; prepare communication plan; assess time for participants to understand material, consult constituents, prepare input; research availability; determine contracting time; number of sessions; time to analyze results and report back; translation time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and interdepartmental coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate internally within the department and coordinate across departments and agencies to ensure consistency and support before engaging stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat other departments as partners, not stakeholders; allow adequate time for review and input; combine consultation activities across departments where possible; inform regional officials and consider coordinating with provincial/territorial governments; consult the government consultation portal for related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting consultation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and select consultation tools appropriate to the size, scope, regional considerations, and stakeholder types; no single tool fits all consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools listed include interviews, hotlines, questionnaires/surveys, open houses/public meetings, conferences/workshops, bilateral meetings, focus groups, advisory boards, comment forms, written submissions, websites/forums, task forces, video conferencing, etc. Engage stakeholders early to help choose tools; consider outreach to underrepresented groups; accommodate accessibility needs (visual/hearing impaired, ethno-cultural, Aboriginal communities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop criteria for selecting participants tailored to the proposal: consider technical/local knowledge, subject-matter expertise, level of impact, and public inclusion where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify roles and responsibilities for officials and stakeholders; design questions carefully; communicate how views will be considered and who is authorized to decide; consider developing a code of conduct for meetings; checklist items: define range of involvement; identify regions to represent; determine availability; research prior consultees; contact key groups for advice; advertise on website or media as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective budgeting for consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Budgeting should be commensurate with the scope: include personnel, time, communications, technical information, logistics, travel, third-party facilitators, participant funding, translation, and IT support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items: determine funds available; consider third-party facilitation; assess adequacy of funds; examine contributions from other departments; evaluate contractors for materials; determine translation needs; decide if independent evaluator required; assess IT support; calculate travel and facility costs; determine cost of notification (advertising, mail-out, website); arrange for participants with special needs; assess intervener funding availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing evaluation (during process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct ongoing evaluation to determine whether the consultation plan is being implemented effectively, whether information gathered is valid and reliable, and whether adjustments are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish evaluation framework and supporting methodologies at design stage; consider neutral observers or subject-matter/external evaluation experts for complex proposals; checklist items: determine tangible results expected; assess key activities; consider neutral observer; assess method appropriateness; evaluate timetable adequacy; develop tracking document; ensure all comments are recorded; determine appropriate number of participants; assess whether stakeholders feel consultation is worthwhile.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-process / final evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of consultations, evaluate success, impact, and results to identify what worked and unanticipated outcomes; measure quality of information and extent to which objectives were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist questions include: Were views as anticipated? Was method effective in engaging groups? Did participants feel process was worthwhile? Did methods suit objectives? Were quantitative/qualitative information and response rates as expected? Was timetable adhered to? Was enough time allowed? Was information used effective and accessible (plain language, other languages/formats)? Was process adequately budgeted? Were supporting materials effective? Was follow-up conducted and input used?

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and tracking of consultation comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all comments are recorded, tracked, and documented so officials can demonstrate how stakeholder views were considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop tracking documents; ensure completeness of records; make documentation available as part of accountability and reporting (e.g., RIAS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback and follow-up to stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform stakeholders about how their input was used and provide reasons when input could not be reflected in the proposed regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow-up maintains trust and helps build ongoing relationships; include reporting mechanisms to show how comments were addressed in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement (RIAS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIAS should be comprehensive and written in simple, clear, concise language understandable to the general public; it must account for how the regulatory proposal followed elements of the Cabinet Directive, including consultations (who was consulted, their views, and how comments were addressed) and a summary of expected impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit draft RIAS to the Secretariat for feedback and to confirm consistency with the Cabinet Directive; use RIAS as a consultation tool when pre-published in Canada Gazette, Part I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-publication comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When draft regulations are pre-published, interested parties are allowed time to express views—usually 30 days. The Cabinet Directive requires a minimum of 75 days for regulations with potential impact on international trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-publication is a final opportunity to obtain comments and to determine whether stakeholders were missed; international agreements may set different comment periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from pre-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited circumstances, an exemption from pre-publication may be granted by the designated Cabinet committee on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage Secretariat analysts early for advice on appropriateness of an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with Aboriginal groups — special considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consulting with Aboriginal groups involves special considerations due to a fiduciary relationship and potential obligations arising from section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982; departments must work with First Nations, Inuit, and Métis communities and organizations and ensure obligations related to protected rights are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure culturally appropriate engagement, consider special outreach and coordination, and meet legal/constitutional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with relevant statutes and Official Languages Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials must ensure regulatory consultations are consistent with all relevant statutes related to the proposed regulations and comply with the Official Languages Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for translation (written and simultaneous) and make materials available in required languages and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating neutral, relevant, and timely information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide timely information in clear, plain language; determine stakeholder knowledge levels and whether learning events are necessary; distribute necessary background materials; decide whether to provide draft regulatory text; include contact names and ensure all stakeholders receive the same information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a code of conduct for consultations and obtain agreement; ensure materials are accessible and objective to encourage informed deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officials’ skills and facilitation capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Officials conducting consultations should have interpersonal and technical skills to manage, facilitate, mediate, and communicate effectively; they must listen, build consensus, manage conflict, and understand decision-making parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key skills/knowledge: consensus building, facilitation, meeting management, negotiation, conflict resolution, problem solving, risk management, information management, communication. Consider skill-based selection of facilitators and training (e.g., courses in facilitation, communication, conflict management, negotiation, mediation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in selecting a consultation facilitator
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting a facilitator consider scope and impact of proposal, differing stakeholder views, potential for conflict, and level of trust stakeholders have in government; facilitator should gain trust, ensure credibility, and have temperament to manage conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex or contentious consultations, consider independent/neutral facilitators and possibly neutral observers for monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation best practices (Checklist 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: In facilitating consultations: share expectations with participants; encourage participants to share expectations; establish participant code of conduct; let participants express viewpoints without officials inserting their own opinions; understand importance of issue for participants; separate problems into components and develop solutions; assess potential for satisfactory resolution and willingness to explore alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these practices to encourage productive dialogue, manage conflict, and produce useful outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate consultation methods — evaluative checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Research previous consultations for methods used; assess advantages/disadvantages of various tools; facilitate stakeholder involvement in selecting tools; determine whether different interest groups should be brought together; assess whether consensus is the goal; ensure tool is appropriate for size and scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the checklist (Checklist 6) as decision support when choosing methods; adapt to stakeholder needs and goals.
